TC_OWNER.description: Mandatory ThreatConnect 'owner' name to pull indicators under. Operators typically pin a single organisation / community / source ('Common Community', 'My Org', 'vendor X feed') so the executor only emits IOCs the operator has access to under that owner. Forwarded into the TQL filter as ownerName EQ "...". Whitespace is trimmed; blank / non-string input aborts the run with a helpful error.

TC_INDICATOR_TYPE.description: Mandatory ThreatConnect indicator type to fetch — one of 'Address' (IPv4/IPv6), 'EmailAddress', 'File' (hashes), 'Host' (FQDN), 'URL'. Forwarded into the TQL filter as typeName EQ "..." so the API itself does the type-narrowing; anything else is rejected client-side with a hard error so a typo doesn't silently pull every indicator type. Operator-friendly aliases (ip / ipv4 / ipv6 / email / fqdn / domain / hash / uri) are normalised onto the canonical title-cased TC type names. ThreatConnect supports more types in the platform (CIDR, ASN, Mutex, Registry Key, User Agent, ...) but this executor's contract is narrowed to the five most-requested types per the playbook spec — operators who need the others should run a separate scan with the appropriate type.

name: threatconnect
title: ThreatConnect Threat Intelligence
description: ThreatConnect Threat Intelligence Platform (TIP) importer. Pulls indicator-of-compromise (IOC) records from the canonical ThreatConnect v3 REST surface (https://api.threatconnect.com/api/v3/indicators and /api/v3/groups) and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. ThreatConnect is a commercial TIP — operators curate IOCs (Address / EmailAddress / File / Host / URL) under named 'owners' (organisation / community / source) and surface them to downstream tools via the v3 REST API. The executor pages /api/v3/indicators with a TQL filter pinning ownerName EQ TC_OWNER and typeName EQ TC_INDICATOR_TYPE and sorts by lastModified desc so the newest IOCs are at the head of the result set; pagination walks resultStart / resultLimit in 500-record pages until either the result set is exhausted, MAX_RESULTS (10000) is reached, or MAX_PAGES (50) is hit. Auth: ThreatConnect uses HMAC-SHA256 signed requests — the operator creates an API key + secret pair in the TC console (Account Settings -> Memberships -> Create API User) and pastes the returned values into TC_ACCESS_ID + TC_SECRET_KEY. The executor constructs the canonical signing string '<URI_PATH>:<HTTP_METHOD>:<UNIX_TIMESTAMP>' (where URI_PATH is the request path + query string starting with /), computes base64(HMAC-SHA256(TC_SECRET_KEY, canonical)) and sends 'Authorization: TC <access_id>:<signature>' + 'Timestamp: <unix_timestamp>' headers on every request. TC_HOST is optional and defaults to https://api.threatconnect.com (the canonical TC cloud host); settable to a regional / dedicated-tenant URL or to a self-hosted on-prem TC instance. Each indicator becomes one Faraday vulnerability under a single synthetic 0.0.0.0 host with hostname 'threatconnect' (TC IOCs are IOC-keyed not host-keyed — the operator's other agents emit the host-side findings this feed is correlated against), tagged exactly ['threatconnect'] per the playbook spec, with a [TC] name prefix, the canonical indicator value + type in the name, and the TC record id in external_id. Severity is bucketed from TC's threatAssessScore (0..1000 proprietary CAL score; higher = more malicious): >=800 critical / >=500 high / >=200 medium / >=50 low / <50 info. Falls back to the rating (1..5) ladder when threatAssessScore is absent: 5 -> critical / 4 -> high / 3 -> medium / 2 -> low / 1 -> info. Inactive indicators (active: false) are floored to 'info' regardless of score — TC operators only mark IOCs inactive after analyst review confirms they're stale. Unscored / unrated records default to 'info'. Status is always open (a TC IOC cannot be 'fixed' in the catalog — it can only be blocked on the operator's perimeter / EDR). Resolution defaults to a type-appropriate blocking recommendation: Address -> firewall + egress proxy + EDR; EmailAddress -> mail-server blocklist + DMARC/quarantine; File -> EDR / AV / endpoint-prevention; Host -> sinkhole + DNS blocklist; URL -> egress proxy + endpoint web-filter. Refs include the canonical TC web-UI permalink, the indicator value, type, owner, rating, confidence, threatAssessScore, every tag, every associated group with its type prefix, every attribute key/value pair, any CVE ids surfaced in attribute values (each with its canonical NVD permalink), the TC record id, dateAdded / lastModified timestamps, and observationCount as explicit Tc-* pivots so operators can pivot from a Faraday finding back to the TC record. Tags: [threatconnect].
